_notes: 10 frames at 200 ms, voice 0.5. Faces of 60 px at x 400 (A, centre 430) and x 1300 (B, centre 1330), both mouths alternating 0.1/0.3.
Both have lips 1 on every frame (each 500 ms window holds 0.1 and 0.3) and score (0.6 + continuity) / 0.65 > 0.5: an overlap on all 10 frames (2 s >= 1.5 s), so it stays an overlap.
Frame 0: equal scores, no priority, so the lower id, p1, becomes the current speaker; B never beats A by 0.15, so p1 holds the frame on every frame.
Both faces don't fit one 608 px window (they span 400 to 1360), so a split. Each split region is round(60 / 0.35) = 171 px tall for a 960 px half: 5.6x, over the 200% limit.
A single window is 1080 px tall for 1920: 1.78x, within the limit. So the segment is single on whoever held the frame, p1, reason overlap. Before this rule it went wide (low-quality).
One cut key on A's centre: x 430, y 540, h 1080, no layout.
